TASK: Make the public marketing site aware of whether the visitor is signed in.

THE REQUIREMENT (from the owner): "the website needs to be able to detect if someone is logged in and if they log in, that info is saved for the next 30 days before they have to log in again. And if they have already logged in, when they are at the marketing page instead of 'Sign in' or 'Get started' the nav menu says 'Portal' and 'Create website'."

## FIRST, VERIFY WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE

I have already checked two of these — confirm both yourself before building:
- `lib/auth.ts:13` sets `SESSION_DAYS = 30` and the session cookie carries a matching `expires`. **So the 30-day persistence already exists.** Verify it end to end: check the cookie attributes actually set (httpOnly, sameSite, secure, path, expires), whether the session is ever extended on activity or is a hard 30 days from sign-in, and whether an expired row is cleaned up. Report exactly what is true. If it is a hard 30 days with no sliding renewal, say so — that is a meaningfully different promise from "30 days since you last used it", and the owner should know which one they have.
- `components/marketing/MarketingNav.tsx` has hardcoded `Sign in` / `Get started` links and never calls `getCurrentUser()`. That is the actual gap.

## WHAT TO BUILD

Make every public marketing surface show the right state:
- Signed OUT: unchanged — "Sign in" and "Get started".
- Signed IN: "Portal" (→ `/dashboard`) and "Create website" (→ `/dashboard/new`).

**The hard part is caching, and it is the whole job.** Read carefully first:
- `MarketingNav.tsx` and every page that renders it: `app/page.tsx`, `app/pricing/page.tsx`, `app/blog/**`, `app/templates/page.tsx`, `app/wizard/page.tsx`, `app/contact/page.tsx`, `app/legal/**`, `app/status/page.tsx`. **Check which of these are statically prerendered** — the build output marks several as `○ (Static)`. A statically prerendered page CANNOT read a cookie, and forcing every marketing page dynamic to render two nav links is a real cost to a site whose whole point is SEO.
- `app/templates/page.tsx` and `app/wizard/page.tsx` already call `getCurrentUser()` and set `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` — read the comments explaining why.
- `proxy.ts` — what already runs on every request.

**Decide the approach deliberately and justify it.** The options are roughly: force the marketing pages dynamic; render the nav client-side from a lightweight `/api/auth/me`-style endpoint (accepting a flash of the signed-out state, which is bad on a hero); or a middleware/proxy-set non-sensitive hint cookie read by an otherwise-static page. Each has real costs — state them, pick one, and say what you traded away. **Do not silently make the entire marketing site dynamic without saying so.**

Whatever you choose must not leak anything sensitive. If you introduce a hint cookie it must contain no identity, no email and no token — only a boolean-ish signal — and it must be kept in sync when someone signs out, or the nav will offer "Portal" to a signed-out visitor and bounce them to `/login`. **Test that sign-out path explicitly**; a stale hint is the obvious failure mode.

Also check `components/marketing/MarketingFooter.tsx` and the auth pages (`app/(auth)/**`) for the same assumption — e.g. whether an already-signed-in visitor hitting `/login` should be redirected.

## HARD RULES
- Do NOT touch `app/(portal)/**`, `app/projects/[id]/**`, `app/admin/**`, `components/ui/**`, `components/app/**`, or `prisma/schema.prisma`. Other agents are working there.
- You MAY edit `components/marketing/**`, `app/page.tsx`, `app/pricing/**`, `app/blog/**`, `app/contact/**`, `app/legal/**`, `app/status/**`, `app/templates/page.tsx`, `app/wizard/page.tsx`, `app/(auth)/**`, `proxy.ts`, and add a route under `app/api/auth/`.
- `lib/auth.ts` — you may ADD to it, but do not change existing behaviour without flagging it loudly.
- Match the existing marketing visual language exactly. This is not a redesign.
- Must pass `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0`, `node --import ./scripts/test/register.mjs --test "tests/*.test.mjs"` (303 currently pass), and `npm run build`. Run all four. **Check the build output and report which marketing routes changed from static to dynamic, if any.**

REPORT BACK: exactly what the session behaviour already was (hard 30 days vs sliding), your caching decision and what it cost, which routes changed static→dynamic, how you keep the signed-out path correct, and anything untested.

content.thinking:
I realize the blog slug page is ISR (force-static with hourly revalidation), which means it can't read cookies at all — making it force-dynamic would break static generation for SEO-critical blog posts. So I'm mapping out which routes are already dynamic versus static versus ISR to figure out the right approach for each.

For the static pages, MarketingNav is a client component, so it could read the non-httpOnly hint cookie via document.cookie during hydration — but that means the initial HTML renders signed-out and flips after hydration, causing a nav flash on static pages. I'm now considering a hybrid: pages already dynamic can pass the auth hint server-side, while static/ISR pages accept the brief client-side flash as a tradeoff.

I'm wondering if that flash can be eliminated entirely using an inline pre-paint script in the head that reads the cookie and sets a class before render, mirroring the theme-flash-prevention approach already in the layout.

That way both signed-in and signed-out nav variants render into HTML, toggled purely by CSS based on that class, avoiding a client-side flip. The tradeoff is duplicated DOM and slight SEO noise, since crawlers would see both link sets and links to authenticated routes could bounce to /login, though that seems like a minor concern.

Since proxy runs without database access, it can only check for the presence of the session cookie, not its validity — meaning if a session gets revoked from another device, the cookie hint would still say "signed in" and the user would click Portal only to be bounced to /login. That's an acceptable edge case though, since the cookie's own expiry aligns with the session expiry anyway.

Actually, I'm reconsidering whether a separate hint cookie is even needed at all, since the session cookie is httpOnly and unreadable by static pages or JS. A cleaner approach might be setting a non-httpOnly hint cookie directly in createSession/destroySession in lib/auth.ts, matching the same expiry, which keeps things in sync at exactly the two moments that matter — though existing logged-in users without that new hint cookie would need the proxy to backfill it until they next log in.

But adding Set-Cookie headers to static/ISR responses risks poisoning CDN caching, so I want to avoid touching the proxy layer for that. Instead I'm leaning toward handling this purely in lib/auth.ts, with MarketingNav falling back to reading the hint cookie client-side via document.cookie on static pages, and accepting a signedIn prop directly on already-dynamic pages where no flash occurs anyway.

For static pages without the hint cookie yet (existing sessions), a hydration-safe check requires useEffect rather than a synchronous initializer, since the latter would mismatch SSR output. I'm weighing whether a brief flash on pages like /pricing, /contact, /legal/*, and /blog/[slug] is acceptable given none of them are the hero page.

The harder problem is backfilling the hint cookie for currently logged-in users on static pages without a proxy-level Set-Cookie -- since server components can't set cookies and being wrong for all existing sessions until next login is unacceptable. So I want to check whether this deployment actually sits behind a CDN or is self-hosted, since if it's self-hosted the proxy Set-Cookie approach becomes safe again; I should check next.config.ts and deploy.sh, confirm whether proxy.ts runs on edge or node runtime, and also look at ThemeToggle's pattern and the auth login page for reference.

Looking at the baseline, tsc shows errors only in forbidden files like the portal layout and a couple other pre-existing spots, so those aren't things I introduced. Eslint similarly flags a handful of warnings confined to those same forbidden areas.

All 303 tests pass, so I know I can't fully clean up tsc/eslint/build without touching files outside my scope — I'll just document that clearly and make sure my own changes don't add new errors.

Now I'm sketching a hybrid design that avoids introducing any new dynamic routes: I'll extend the auth module additively with a hint cookie constant and wire it into session creation and destruction so the app can detect auth state without forcing dynamic rendering everywhere.

Since modifying createSession's behavior technically counts as a change I'm supposed to flag, I'll call it out explicitly, but this is still the right choke point since it's the single place sign-in and sign-out happen, keeping the hint reliably in sync.

I'm also planning proxy-level logic to reconcile the session cookie and the new hint cookie on each request — setting the hint if a session exists but the hint is missing, and clearing it if the session is gone but the hint lingers — while making sure this only fires when they're out of sync so it doesn't interfere with ISR caching on the blog pages.

Since the proxy can't read the real database expiry when backfilling, I'm reasoning through what expiry to give the hint cookie so any mismatch self-corrects on the next request rather than causing stale signed-in/signed-out UI flashes.

I realize proxy.ts can't import from lib/auth.ts because that pulls in the prisma db client into the proxy bundle, so I need a separate small module holding just the cookie name and max-age constants with no dependencies, shared by lib/auth.ts, proxy.ts, and the client nav.  Since this new file isn't listed as forbidden, adding `lib/auth-hint.ts` seems safe. Now I'm thinking through the `MarketingNav` component's props, particularly using an authoritative server-provided `signedIn` boolean where possible.

For static pages without that prop, falling back to reading the cookie client-side in an effect causes a one-frame flash since the prerendered HTML shows the signed-out state before flipping to "Portal." I'm weighing whether a CSS-driven swap could avoid this flash more cheaply than duplicating the theme's inline-script trick, but that adds complexity to render both variants at once — I'm leaning toward accepting the minor flash for simplicity on static pages.

I could extend that existing theme script to also set a signed-in class based on the auth cookie, then render both auth states in the nav and use CSS to show/hide based on that class rather than a JS conditional — eliminating the flash entirely since it resolves before first paint.

Cookies

Kodely sets three cookies, and every one of them is strictly necessary:

  • kodely_session keeps you signed in for up to 30 days. It holds a random token, and the corresponding record in our database holds only a hash of it, so a database read never yields a usable cookie.
  • kodely_google_oauth_state is set only when you click “Sign in with Google”, lives ten minutes, and exists to prove the reply from Google answers your own request rather than someone else's forgery.
  • kodely_discord_reward_state does the same job, only when you choose to connect a Discord account for reward credits.

There is no advertising pixel, no third-party analytics cookie and no tracker that follows you to another site — which is why you are not shown a cookie banner. The full reasoning, and what your browser stores locally, is on{" "} Your data and your rights.

Technical data

Cookie What it does Lifetime
kodely_session Keeps you signed in. Holds a random token; the database stores only a hash of it. HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure. 30 days
kodely_google_oauth_state Set only when you click “Sign in with Google”. Carries a one-time value that proves the reply from Google answers your request and not someone else's forgery. Deleted the moment you come back. 10 minutes
kodely_discord_reward_state The same thing, set only when you choose to connect Discord for reward credits. 10 minutes

That is the entire list. All three are strictly necessary — two of them are security measures, and the third is what being signed in is. There is no advertising pixel, no Google Analytics, no third-party tag manager, no fingerprinting script, and no cookie that follows you to another site. A banner over that set would ask you to agree to nothing, would change nothing whichever button you pressed, and would teach you that clicking through dialogs is the price of reading a page. We would rather publish the list.

Your browser also keeps three things locally that never reach our servers: your light/dark preference, whether you have dismissed the first-run checklist, and — if you typed a prompt on the homepage before signing in — that prompt, held until the project is created for you. Clearing your browser storage for kodely.me removes all three.

content.text:
All four gates pass. Here's the report.

## 1. What the 30-day session actually was (verified end to end, not just read)

**It is a hard 30 days from sign-in, with no sliding renewal.** Confirmed empirically: I signed in a throwaway account, hit `/templates` and `/api/auth/me` with the session, and re-read the row — `expiresAt` was byte-identical before and after. `getCurrentUser()` only ever *reads* the row; nothing writes a new expiry.

That is a meaningfully weaker promise than "30 days since you last used it": **a user who logs in daily is still forced to re-authenticate on day 31.** The owner should know which one they're shipping.

- `lib/auth.ts:13` `SESSION_DAYS = 30` ✓. Row `expiresAt = now + 30d`; cookie `expires` set to the *same* Date — measured 30.000 days out, and the cookie and row can't drift.
- Cookie attributes, observed live off the wire: `HttpOnly` ✓, `SameSite=Lax` ✓, `Path=/` ✓, `Secure` only when `NODE_ENV=production` ✓. Token is 32 random bytes; the DB stores only a SHA-256 hash.
- **Expired rows are not cleaned up on the auth path.** `getCurrentUser`/`getCurrentSession` return `null` past expiry but leave the row. A purge exists — `purgeExpiredSessions` in `lib/retention.ts` (`SESSION_GRACE_DAYS = 0`) — but it only runs when someone manually invokes `node scripts/retention.mjs --only sessions --apply`; `docs/retention.md` confirms there is no cron. So `Session` grows unboundedly in practice.

## 2. Caching decision, and what it cost

The decisive constraint is `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` — `force-static` + `revalidate = 3600`. Forcing that dynamic to render two nav links would put a server render and a session lookup in front of every blog post, which is the entire SEO surface.

**I used a hybrid, and no marketing route changed status:**

- Pages already rendered per request (`/`, `/blog`, `/templates`, `/wizard`, `/status`) receive `signedIn` as a prop from `getCurrentUser()`. The correct nav is **in the first byte of HTML — no flash**, and it's authoritative (a stale cookie can't override it).
- Statically prerendered pages (`/pricing`, `/contact`, `/legal/*`, `/blog/[slug]`) resolve it in the browser from a hint cookie, via `useSignedIn` — built on `useSyncExternalStore` with a `null` server snapshot, exactly the pattern `ThemeToggle` already uses here. Verified in a real browser: no hydration warnings.

**What I traded away:** a one-paint flash of the signed-out nav on those four static surfaces. It is deliberately confined to pages with no hero and no above-the-fold CTA — the homepage, the one page where a flash would be unacceptable, is on the authoritative path.

The hint cookie (`kodely_auth`) contains **only the literal `1`** — no id, no email, no token, asserted by test. It grants nothing: every real gate is still `getCurrentUser()`.

## 3. Routes that changed static → dynamic

**Zero marketing routes.** `/pricing`, `/contact`, `/legal/{privacy,terms,rights}` and `/blog/[slug]` all remain `○ (Static)`; `/`, `/blog`, `/templates`, `/wizard`, `/status` were already `ƒ`.

**Two auth routes changed, both mine and both intentional:** `/login` and `/signup` went `○ → ƒ`. I verified they were `○` beforehand by rebuilding with the session read removed. They now redirect an already-signed-in visitor — to `/continue`, *not* `/dashboard`, because `PromptHero` stashes a typed prompt in `sessionStorage` and throws people at `/signup`; `/continue` is the existing page that converts that into a project, so redirecting straight to `/dashboard` would silently discard someone's prompt. The check is `getCurrentUser()` rather than the hint **specifically to avoid a redirect loop** — a stale hint driving this would bounce /login → portal → /login forever.

## 4. Keeping the signed-out path correct (tested explicitly)

Three layers, all exercised against a live server — 40 assertions, all passing:

- `destroySession()` deletes the hint in the same function as the session, so sign-out has one implementation and can't forget. Verified: logout returns `Set-Cookie` deletions for *both*, both `Path=/`.
- `proxy.ts` repairs disagreement on every request: session-without-hint → set (backfills the ~30 days of sessions that predate this), **hint-without-session → clear**. Verified in-browser: deleting only the session cookie left a stale hint offering "Portal"; the very next request cleared it and the nav reverted to "Sign in"/"Get started".
- Only the two *disagreeing* rows touch the response. Confirmed an anonymous request to `/pricing` and `/blog` gets **no `Set-Cookie` at all** — that's what keeps the cached pages cacheable.

I also updated `app/legal/privacy` and `app/legal/rights`, which enumerate every cookie and *count* them ("Kodely sets three cookies", "That is the entire list. All three…"). Adding a fourth without touching those would have made the published privacy policy false.

## 5. Deliberately not done, and open risks

- **The homepage still redirects signed-in visitors to `/dashboard`** (`app/page.tsx:20`, pre-existing). I did **not** remove it. The owner's wording implies a signed-in visitor should *see* the marketing home with a "Portal" nav, but `PromptHero` unconditionally routes to `/signup` and the hero CTAs are all built for the signed-out funnel — removing the redirect without rewiring those creates a worse bug than it fixes. One line to change if the owner wants it; flagging rather than deciding silently.
- **In-body CTAs still say "Get started" → `/signup`** on `/pricing` (credit packs) and `/blog/[slug]`. The requirement was the nav menu. The pricing packs in particular should probably go to checkout for a signed-in user — a separate, larger decision.
- **A session revoked from another device** leaves a hint this browser still trusts until its cookie expires: that visitor sees "Portal" and gets bounced to `/login`. Unavoidable without a DB read on static pages; self-correcting and non-security-relevant.
- **Untested:** the `pageshow`/`visibilitychange`/`focus` resubscribe in `useSignedIn` (the sign-out-in-another-tab case) — the parse it depends on is unit-tested, but I did not drive two tabs. Also untested: behaviour behind a CDN. There is none today (`next start` on a VM), but a CDN caching the backfill `Set-Cookie` on an ISR blog response would be a problem worth checking before one is introduced.
- **Note on the tree:** the baseline build was already failing on `app/projects/[id]/Editor.tsx`, `components/app/AppShell.tsx` and `app/(portal)/layout.tsx` — other agents' in-flight work, all off-limits to me. Those were fixed by their owners mid-task; final `tsc`, `eslint`, tests (**315 pass**, 303 + 12 new in `tests/auth-hint.test.mjs`) and `npm run build` are all clean.
